# reading-group@local.edu — postfix + mailman3

## Layout

| Piece | Path |
|---|---|
| Mailman config | `/etc/mailman3/mailman.cfg` |
| List database | `/var/lib/mailman3/data/mailman.db` (sqlite) |
| Postfix transport maps | `/var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp{,.db}` |
| Address-extension fallback | `/etc/postfix/mailman_transport.regexp` |
| Mailman logs | `/var/log/mailman3/{mailman,smtp}.log` |
| Postfix log | `/var/log/mail.log` |
| User mailboxes | `/var/mail/<username>` (mbox) |
| Start/stop helper | `/usr/local/bin/mail-services` |
| Provisioner | `/app/provision.sh` |

## Mail flow

```
user --:25--> postfix --LMTP 127.0.0.1:8024--> mailman
              mailman --:25 SMTP--> postfix --> /var/mail/<user>
```

Postfix treats `local.edu` as a local domain, but `transport_maps` overrides
every `reading-group*@local.edu` address to `lmtp:127.0.0.1:8024`, so list
traffic goes to Mailman while ordinary `<user>@local.edu` mail is still
delivered locally to `/var/mail/<user>`.

`transport_maps` also includes `regexp:/etc/postfix/mailman_transport.regexp`
so that address-extension forms match:
`reading-group-confirm+<cookie>@local.edu` — the reply address Mailman puts in
the `From:` of confirmation mails (the "friendly" VERP confirmation scheme,
`mta.verp_confirmations: yes`) — and `reading-group-bounces+...@local.edu`.

## List behaviour

* `reading-group@local.edu` — post an announcement; distributed to all members.
  Both members and non-members may post (`default_*_action = accept`).
* `reading-group-join@local.edu` (alias `-subscribe`) — subscribes the sender
  after they reply to the confirmation mail. `subscription_policy = open`, so
  no list-owner approval is needed.
* `reading-group-leave@local.edu` (alias `-unsubscribe`) — unsubscribes the
  sender after they reply to the confirmation mail
  (`unsubscription_policy = confirm`).
* Any reply to `reading-group-confirm+<cookie>@local.edu` counts as
  confirmation; the cookie is read from the `To:` header.

## Operations

```sh
/usr/local/bin/mail-services start|stop|restart|status
sh /app/provision.sh          # idempotent rebuild from scratch
python3 /app/eval.py         # provided smoke test
```

The container has no init system (PID 1 is `sleep infinity`), so Mailman is
started detached via `setsid` by `mail-services`; nothing restarts it
automatically after a container restart — run `mail-services start`.

## Notes

* Files under `/var/mail` must be owned by their user. A `root`-owned mailbox
  makes postfix fail local delivery with `cannot update mailbox ... Permission
  denied` (it will not follow a hardlink/symlink to a file it does not own), so
  read mailboxes only via `mailbox.mbox(path)` after delivery, never by
  creating them as root.
* Mailman's list attributes are stored through Storm transactions: a plain
  script assigning to `mlist` must wrap the change in
  `with mailman.database.transaction.transaction():` or it is not committed.

* Files under `/var/mail` must be owned by their user. A `root`-owned mailbox
  makes postfix fail local delivery with `cannot update mailbox ... Permission
  denied` (it will not follow a hardlink/symlink to a file it does not own), so
  read mailboxes only via `mailbox.mbox(path)` after delivery, never by
  creating them as root.
* Mailman's list attributes are stored through Storm transactions: a plain
  script assigning to `mlist` must wrap the change in
  `with mailman.database.transaction.transaction():` or it is not committed.
